title: Double-Free via Copy of Owners
pattern: Implementing the Copy trait on a type that owns a heap pointer, file descriptor, or other system resource that has a custom Drop implementation.
why_bad: When the value is reassigned, a bitwise copy is made. Both instances will independently believe they own the resource and will call the destructor, leading to double-free or undefined behavior.
detection: A struct or enum is annotated with `#[derive(Copy)]` (or implements `Copy`) and also implements `Drop` (or contains elements that implement `Drop`).
counterexample: Implementing Clone instead of Copy, forcing explicit duplication of the owned resource handle.
fix: Remove the `Copy` implementation, forcing moves instead, or wrap the resource handle in an `Arc` to share ownership safely.
source: Rust For Rustaceans, Chapter 2 (Drop Order & Copy) [388-389].
